newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds try to push on the U.S.-led rally.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds try to push on the U.S.-led rally.

text.p: *Australian bond yields started lower with the market
attempting to push on the rally seen in after hours trading on
the back of a strong advance in U.S. Treasuries.
*June, Q2 retail trade due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond yields started lower with the market attempting to push on the rally seen in after hours trading on the back of Wednesday's strong advance in U.S. Treasuries.

The U.S. market saw a broad brush of buying interest which took the yield on the 30-year bond down to a 1-1/2 year low of 6.32 percent at one stage amid a back drop of benign inflation, reduced supply and a strengthening U.S. dollar.
Traders said the U.S. move helped to buoy the local debt market which had been under attack from profit-taking on Wednesday after the 1/2 point cut in official rates.

The move to 5.0 percent official rates by the Reserve Bank had been well anticipated for some time, although the actual timing of the announcement was around a week earlier than analysts had generally expected.

Analysts are now weighing up whether this is the last easing in the cycle, although bill futures are already trading below the new official cash rate. The December contract at a day's high of 95.14 equates to a cash rate of 4.86 percent.
June and second quarter retail trade reports are due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), although the data is now somewhat dated given that the rate cut is already in place, analysts said.

Median forecasts centre on a 0.4 percent rise in June retail sales after the 2.9 percent rise in May, while the quarterly figure is seen up 0.1 percent after the 2.2 percent growth in the first quarter, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
Treasurer Peter Costello is due to address the Economic Society in Melbourne at around 1.15 p.m. (0315 GMT).
The market showed an outperforming bias against the dollar
bloc in early trading, although this was more so at the long end
and caused the yield curve to give up some of Wednesday's
steepening which followed the rate cut.
